brief: Hungarian PSPs, EMIs and payment fintechs disclose in two disconnected modes and almost never in a bank-shaped one: audited Hungarian-language annual accounts filed once a year to the state e-beszámoló portal, and irregular, marketing-driven press releases or media-relayed claims about volumes, customers and funding — no quarterly IR cadence was found anywhere in this cell. The reliable spine is therefore governmental: MNB's Intézménykereső and payment-institution/EMI registers to enumerate and name the actors, e-beszámoló for their audited financials, and MNB payment statistics as the market denominator against which self-reported growth claims (SimplePay, B-Payment, Revolut HU) can be sanity-checked. The narrative layer sits with issuer press centres (Barion's is the strongest example) and a small, dense Hungarian trade press — FinTechZone, Portfolio, Forbes.hu, vg.hu, Telex — which is often the only channel where English-first or passported players such as Revolut, Wise, PayU and Pay10 say anything Hungary-specific at all. The main structural risk is cross-border entities: they serve Hungary heavily while filing next to nothing locally, so home-state group reporting must be wired in alongside the domestic registers.
